speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you've recently used any drugs, taken any new medications, or been exposed to any unusual chemicals? Also, have you experienced any fever, tremors, or muscle rigidity over the last few hours?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient's roommates report that he has been displaying increasingly aggressive and unusual behavior. They mention that he has been under significant stress due to final exams and has become more reclusive. Earlier this evening, he exhibited extreme irritability, yelled at his computer, broke it, and then spent several hours at the gym.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you currently feel unusually hot, have a racing heart, or experience heavy sweating? I also need to know if you have consumed any stimulants like cocaine, amphetamines, or energy drinks recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive behavior and irritability. I also have Yelling, Breaking objects, Prolonged physical activity (several hours at the gym), Rapid speech during exam, Aggressiveness during exam.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of bipolar disorder, or have you ever experienced similar episodes of extreme energy and irritability before? I need to know if you are currently taking any mood stabilizers or antipsychotic medications.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported by the roommates. Social history: Stress from upcoming final exams. No other social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any muscle rigidity, confusion, or a very high fever right now? I also need to know if you've been taking any new supplements or medications that your roommates aren't aware of. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Toxicology Screen.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 101°F (38.3°C), Blood Pressure 137/98 mmHg, Heart Rate 120/min, Respiratory Rate 23/min, Oxygen Saturation 99% on room air. General Examination: Irritable appearance, notable diaphoresis. Cardiopulmonary: Tachycardia, bilateral clear breath sounds. Neurological: Notably dilated pupils, rapid speech, aggressive mental status. Toxicology Screen: Amphetamines Positive, Cocaine Negative, Opiates Negative, Benzodiazepines Negative, Cannabinoids Negative. Complete Blood Count: WBC Normal, Hemoglobin Normal, Platelets Normal. Chemistry Panel: Sodium Normal, Potassium Normal, Creatinine Normal, Blood Glucose Normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the positive amphetamine screen, fever, tachycardia, and altered mental status, I need to rule out life-threatening complications. Do you have any history of seizures, or have you noticed any muscle rigidity or confusion in the last few hours? REQUEST TEST: CT Head, Serum CK, Lactic Acid.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Head: No acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or infarction. Serum CK: 4500 U/L (Elevated). Lactic Acid: 4.2 mmol/L (Elevated).

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your elevated CK, lactic acid, fever, and agitation with a positive amphetamine screen, I must ask: have you experienced any severe muscle pain, dark urine, or a feeling of your muscles locking up? I am also checking if you have been drinking fluids recently to rule out severe dehydration. DIAGNOSIS READY: Amphetamine-induced Serotonin Syndrome with Rhabdomyolysis.
